run.question:
Alertmanager alert RequestErrorRate (severity warning) is firing for service otel-demo/frontend-proxy since 2026-11-15T11:18:58Z.
Investigate why this alert is firing.

report.summary: The RequestErrorRate alert on otel-demo/frontend-proxy is fired by the real error burst the proxy sees on its edge spans: frontend-proxy's ERROR-status span rate went from ~0.006-0.008/s before the incident to 1.958/s in the 5-minute window ending 11:27:58 (all of it on its 'ingress' and 'router frontend egress' spans). That burst is a passthrough of a failure inside its only upstream, frontend: frontend's own ERROR spans are exactly the /api/data request chain (GET /api/data -> executing api route (pages) /api/data -> grpc.oteldemo.AdService/GetAds, identical rates), and essentially every GET /api/data span in the affected minutes is an error. The deepest verifiable cause is the ad service: pod ad-554b849958-fcl25's 'ad' container was OOMKilled (exit 137, reason OOMKilled, finished 2026-11-15T11:18:27Z, restarts=1, new instance started 11:18:28Z), and after that restart the service stopped serving: its own GetAds server-span rate fell to 0 and stayed 0, its per-request log stream ends at 11:18:24Z, while the restarted container burns CPU at exactly its 50m limit (0.0495 cores) and its working set climbs from 2.6MB to ~378MB. From ~11:20 the frontend's outbound tcp.connect spans are 100% ERROR (baseline 0), i.e. its gRPC connections to ad fail. ad did not restart again and is not affected by node pressure (node i-06e4f0f4f681d7e45 Ready, no MemoryPressure). Kubernetes surface state is misleading: the ad pod reports Ready and is in the ad Service Endpoints (100.96.4.112:8080) while serving nothing, because the ad Deployment defines no readiness or liveness probe. The remaining unknown is why the restarted ad process never starts serving; the evidence supports CPU-saturation/stall at the 50m quota as the mechanism, not something I could observe inside the container.

claims.text: frontend-proxy's ERROR-status span rate rose from ~0.006-0.008/s (10:54:58-11:19:58) to 1.958/s in the 5-minute window ending 11:27:58, then 1.635/s at 11:28:58 and 1.270/s at 11:29:58; the error spans are on span_name 'ingress' and 'router frontend egress' (STATUS_CODE_ERROR), while the same span names keep ~9-11/s STATUS_CODE_UNSET spans.

Across services, the only large ERROR-span rate increases at the same time are frontend (0 before 11:19:58, 1.054/s at 11:20:58, up to 3.983/s at 11:27:58) and frontend-proxy (up to 1.958/s); accounting, checkout and payment report 0 ERROR rate throughout, and ad/fraud-detection/recommendation only show sporadic ~0.004/s noise.

In frontend, the ERROR spans are confined to one call chain: span_name 'GET', 'GET /api/data', 'executing api route (pages) /api/data' and the outbound client span 'grpc.oteldemo.AdService/GetAds' all carry identical error rates (0.226/s at 11:20:00 rising to ~1.0-1.1/s from 11:23:00), while 'GET /api/cart', 'POST /api/checkout', 'grpc.oteldemo.CartService/GetCart', 'grpc.oteldemo.CartService/AddItem' and 'grpc.oteldemo.CheckoutService/PlaceOrder' are 0.

frontend's total 'GET /api/data' span rate (~0.97-1.1/s) and its 'GET /api/data' ERROR span rate are practically identical from the 11:23:00 window onward (e.g. 1.022/s total vs 1.007/s error at 11:23:00; 1.100/s vs 1.100/s at 11:27:00), i.e. the requests that reach that route are failing.

The ad service stopped handling requests: its server spans 'oteldemo.AdService/GetAds', 'getAdsByCategory' and 'getRandomAds' (STATUS_CODE_UNSET) decline and reach 0 by the 11:22:58 window and stay 0 through 11:29:58; a 1-minute rate of 'oteldemo.AdService/GetAds' is non-zero through the 11:19:15 evaluation and 0 from the 11:19:30 evaluation onward through 11:27:00.

frontend's outbound connection attempts started failing at the same time: ERROR-status spans named 'tcp.connect' were 0 at every evaluation from 11:05:00 to 11:19:58, then 0.033/s at 11:20:00 and up to 0.055/s at 11:24:00, while UNSET-status 'tcp.connect' spans are 0.

Pod otel-demo/ad-554b849958-fcl25 (owner ReplicaSet ad-554b849958) shows container 'ad' lastState.terminated reason OOMKilled, exitCode 137, finishedAt 2026-11-15T11:18:27Z, restarts 1, currently running since 2026-11-15T11:18:28Z, ready true, all pod conditions True.
The ad pod's container events in the window are only Pulled, Created and Started (11:18:27-11:18:28Z); no Evicted, Unhealthy or failed-scheduling event is returned for it.

The ad container's per-request log stream ends at 2026-11-15T11:18:24.817Z (newest of 340 lines read for 11:15:00-11:30:23Z; lines are 'Targeted ad request received ...', 'Non-targeted ad request received ...', 'no baggage found in context').

The restarted ad container (cAdvisor series name ed742b6451d6...) runs at 0.0495 cores/s CPU from ~11:19:30 to ~11:25:30, i.e. pinned at the Deployment's limits.cpu 50m, versus ~0.005 cores/s for the pre-restart instance; the pre-restart instance spiked to 0.019 cores/s just before it was killed.
The ad Deployment sets resources limits cpu 50m / memory 450Mi and requests cpu 10m / memory 225Mi, and defines no readinessProbe and no livenessProbe for the 'ad' container.

Memory evidence around the kill: the pre-restart ad container's working set rose to 420,438,016 bytes at the 11:18:30 sample (container_memory_max_usage_bytes 420,843,520 for that instance) after ~301-310MB earlier, while the restarted instance starts at 2,596,864 bytes (11:18:30) and climbs to ~373-378MB (max_usage 378,281,984).

The ad Service selector is opentelemetry.io/name=ad on TCP 8080, and its Endpoints subset lists pod ad-554b849958-fcl25 at 100.96.4.112:8080; the ad Deployment reports replicas 1 / readyReplicas 1 / availableReplicas 1.
Node i-06e4f0f4f681d7e45 (the node of the ad pod) is Ready (KubeletReady True) with MemoryPressure, DiskPressure and PIDPressure all False at query time.

Only two pods in otel-demo carry restarts or a last termination: ad-554b849958-fcl25 (OOMKilled, 11:18:27Z) and fraud-detection-9fb7d885b-wbm7f (OOMKilled, 10:55:59Z, both ready with restarts 1); frontend-675fd7b5c5-cmhqq and frontend-proxy-6b4d584985-whhck are Running/Ready with 0 restarts and start times 2026-11-15T10:41:23Z / 10:41:25Z.

flagd, the flag backend used by the demo, is healthy in this window: pod flagd-54b69c4c98-mb2t5 Running/Ready with containers flagd and flagd-ui at 0 restarts; and the flagd-config ConfigMap defines adFailure, adHighCpu and adManualGc with defaultVariant 'off'.

Metric discovery shows only two series for frontend-proxy, traces_span_metrics_calls_total and traces_span_metrics_duration_milliseconds_bucket, and a {__name__=~"http_.*|.*request.*"} search listed only cluster:namespace:pod_cpu:active:kube_pod_container_resource_requests and the memory equivalent; no HTTP server request-duration series were returned.

Jaeger lists ad and frontend among the 18 services it has seen, but no traces were returned for frontend in 11:10-11:19 or 11:24-11:30, nor for ad in 11:15-11:30, so no span-level gRPC error message was available from this source.

Primary mechanism: after the 11:18:27 OOM kill the restarted ad container never resumed serving. The new container starts, is Ready (no probes exist) and consumes CPU exactly at its 50m quota (0.0495 cores/s) while its working set climbs to ~378MB, but it produces no per-request log lines after 11:18:24 and no server spans at all, so frontend's gRPC calls to ad fail at the connection level (tcp.connect ERROR spans from ~11:20) and the failure propagates to /api/data, frontend-proxy ingress and this alert.

Trigger / contributing condition: the ad container's memory demand approached its 450Mi limit (working set 420,438,016 bytes and max_usage 420,843,520 bytes recorded for the killed instance), which produced the OOMKilled termination with exit 137; the 450Mi memory limit and 50m CPU limit are very tight for this workload, so the kill started the outage and the small CPU quota plausibly kept the restarted process from recovering.

Open alternative: a runtime fault-injection flag on ad (flagd defines adHighCpu, adManualGc and adFailure, all defaultVariant 'off' in the ConfigMap) could be driving the CPU-saturated, non-serving state; flagd runtime state is not readable here, so this cannot be confirmed or excluded.

Surface Kubernetes state contradicts 'ad is unavailable': pod ad-554b849958-fcl25 reports Ready True with all conditions True, its container is running (0 restarts since 11:18:28), the Deployment reports readyReplicas 1 / availableReplicas 1, and the Endpoints object lists the pod IP 100.96.4.112:8080. Because the Deployment defines no readiness or liveness probe, Ready only means the container process exists, so it cannot detect the stalled process that is visible in the zero spans, zero request logs and CPU pinned at the 50m quota.

Rejected: the frontend application itself is broken. Its error spans are exclusively the outbound 'grpc.oteldemo.AdService/GetAds' client span and the /api/data chain that wraps it, all of its other downstream calls are at 0 error rate, and the frontend pod has been running with 0 restarts since 10:41:23Z.

Rejected: node-level pressure or eviction killed the ad workload. The ad pod is on node i-06e4f0f4f681d7e45, which is Ready with MemoryPressure/DiskPressure/PIDPressure all False, and the pod's termination is recorded as a container OOMKilled (exit 137) with only Pulled/Created/Started events, not an Evicted event.

Rejected: ad was rolled out or rescheduled to a replacement pod. The same pod name ad-554b849958-fcl25 is still running under ReplicaSet ad-554b849958 with restarts 1 (in-place container restart), and the only events are Pulled/Created/Started of the 'ad' container at 11:18:27-28Z.

Rejected: a flagd outage cut the ad service off. The flagd pod is Running with both containers Ready and 0 restarts, and ad's only pre-existing flagd-related error signal (span 'flagd.evaluation.v1.Service/EventStream' ERROR at ~0.004/s) was also present before the incident.

Rejected: the earlier fraud-detection OOMKilled restart (10:55:59Z) caused this alert. It occurred ~23 minutes before the error onset, fraud-detection is not on the failing /api/data -> AdService path, and its ERROR span rate stayed at 0 apart from sporadic ~0.004/s noise.

Treat ad as the failing dependency: raise/adjust the ad container's resources (limits.cpu 50m and limits.memory 450Mi are very tight for a restarted .NET service) and inspect the running ad process (its listener state and any GC/CPU loop) — a simple restart of pod ad-554b849958-fcl25 is the fastest way to test whether the stalled instance is the cause.

Add a readiness probe (and a liveness probe) to the ad Deployment: the current pod reports Ready and stays in the ad Service Endpoints while serving no requests, so Kubernetes cannot route around or restart a stalled ad process.

gaps: The alerting rule 'RequestErrorRate' is not loaded in this Prometheus (list_prometheus_rules by rule_name returned no data), so the alert's exact expression, threshold and the metric behind the annotation value 1.5333333333333332 could not be verified; the untrusted annotation's magnitude is only consistent with the observed frontend-proxy ERROR span rates (1.635/s at 11:28:58).

No span-level error message (gRPC status/code) was obtainable: Jaeger lists ad and frontend but returned no traces for frontend in 11:10-11:19 and 11:24-11:30 or for ad in 11:15-11:30, so the exact client-side error text of grpc.oteldemo.AdService/GetAds is unknown.

The restarted ad container produced no log lines that the log tool returned for 11:18:25-11:30:23 (that query returned no_data, which is not proof of absence), and the frontend container returned no log lines at all (0 bytes read), so no application-level error text is available for either side.

Why the restarted ad process does not serve could not be observed directly: there is no exec/process inspection, container_cpu_cfs_throttled_* series were not present (no_data) and container_spec_memory_limit_bytes returned no data, so CPU throttling and the effective cgroup memory limit are inferred from the Deployment spec and cadvisor usage series only.
flagd runtime flag values could not be read (only the flagd-config ConfigMap defaults, which are 'off'), so a runtime adHighCpu/adManualGc/adFailure injection cannot be confirmed or excluded.
The change_history integration is not available, so no deploy, config or flag-change record exists to explain the 11:18:27 OOM or the post-restart behaviour.

No ERROR-status series were returned for cart, currency, product-catalog, quote, shipping, email, image-provider or kafka, so their error state is unknown rather than proven zero; only accounting, checkout and payment were observed at 0 ERROR rate.
next_steps: Inspect the running ad container directly (process state, listening socket on 8080, thread/GC activity) and its memory/cpu cgroup counters to confirm why the restarted process does not serve.
Check whether ad's memory limit (450Mi) was exceeded by an organic demand spike or a leak, and consider raising limits.memory/limits.cpu for the ad Deployment.
Add readiness/liveness probes to the ad Deployment so that a container that starts but never serves is removed from the Service Endpoints and restarted.
Verify in flagd whether adHighCpu, adManualGc or adFailure were enabled at runtime around 11:18, since the ConfigMap only shows defaults.
Locate the actual RequestErrorRate alerting rule (it is not in this Prometheus) to confirm which metric and window the alert evaluates.
